previous_description: Defines validation rules for JSON numeric instances (number or integer types), including inclusive/exclusive bounds and divisibility constraints. Note: in JSON Schema Draft 7, exclusiveMinimum and exclusiveMaximum are numeric boundary values (e.g., exclusiveMinimum: 0), not the boolean flags used in Draft 4.
definition: A schema constraining JSON number or integer values through validation keywords: inclusive or exclusive lower and upper bounds, or a divisibility step (multipleOf). It describes the value space of a numeric datum, independent of the field that carries it or how the value is stored.

distinguish_from.when: the element is a named field of an object (e.g. Order.quantity) carrying its own title, default, readOnly or description; the numeric constraints it applies may be modelled as a NumericSchema that the property references.
the numeric type is a named, reusable definition under 'definitions' (e.g. a 'Percentage' type referenced via $ref), especially one restricted to an enum of fixed values rather than a range.
the value is serialized as a string even though it looks numeric, e.g. a decimal-as-string money amount, a zero-padded code or a phone number constrained by pattern or length.
the numeric constraint is formed by combining subschemas with allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not, e.g. 'positive OR null', rather than by a single set of bounds.

standard_reference: JSON Schema Draft 7 Validation §6.2 Validation Keywords for Numeric Instances (multipleOf, maximum, exclusiveMaximum, minimum, exclusiveMinimum), with type 'number'/'integer' (§6.1.1)
code_evidence: a JSON Schema or OpenAPI fragment with "type": "integer" or "number" plus minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum or multipleOf keywords
a numeric field annotated with range validators, e.g. Java @Min/@Max/@DecimalMin/@Positive, Pydantic Field(ge=0, le=100) or conint(gt=0), or Zod z.number().int().min(1)
a declared numeric value type or constrained alias with range checks in its constructor or validator, e.g. a Percentage or Quantity class that rejects values outside 0..100 or non-integers

attribute_descriptions.name: minimum
attribute_descriptions.description: Inclusive lower bound: valid instances must be greater than or equal to this number, in the same units as the value. Set it when the domain forbids smaller values, e.g. 0 for quantities.

attribute_descriptions.name: maximum
attribute_descriptions.description: Inclusive upper bound: valid instances must be less than or equal to this number, in the same units as the value. Set it when the domain caps the value, e.g. 100 for a percentage.

attribute_descriptions.name: exclusiveMinimum
attribute_descriptions.description: Exclusive lower bound given as a number (Draft 7 semantics): valid instances must be strictly greater than this value. Set it instead of minimum when the boundary itself is invalid, e.g. 0 for a strictly positive price.

attribute_descriptions.name: exclusiveMaximum
attribute_descriptions.description: Exclusive upper bound given as a number (Draft 7 semantics): valid instances must be strictly less than this value. Set it instead of maximum when the boundary itself is invalid, e.g. 1 for a probability strictly below one.

attribute_descriptions.name: multipleOf
attribute_descriptions.description: Strictly positive number that every valid instance must divide into evenly, expressing a step or precision such as 0.01 for cents or 5 for five-minute intervals. Set it only when the domain imposes such a granularity.

notes: Unlike StringSchema and ArraySchema, 'type' here is a required enum; align siblings, which use 'any'. No 'format' attribute exists for int32/int64/float/double hints, which OpenAPI-derived code commonly carries. Overlap with SchemaProperty, whose type enum includes number/integer: specify whether inline field bounds create a separate NumericSchema element or stay on the property.
